arcs.description: The whole file. An arc is one layer of the Columbia openness ontology (the GPAIS tech stack) plus a display label for it and an ordered list of the categories that sit in it; three arcs hold all 16 categories as of 2026-08-08. This is the ONLY place a category's position in the stack is declared, and it is hand-edited: whoever adds a category or reorders the map writes it, never a tool. Everything downstream is derived from it and stored nowhere else: build/serialize.py flattens the arcs in sequence into the payload's `order`, stamps each category with its arc `name` and `layer`, and emits the arc sequence as `layer_order`; build/serialize_registry.py writes `arc_name` and `layer` into the registry's categories.csv, which warehouse/ingest/build_stack_map.py joins so every scored repo carries a layer in the warehouse. The schema is deliberately loose here (it does not require the array to be non-empty, and it cannot compare one arc against another), so the real invariants are cross-file and live in build/validate.py: every category file appears in exactly one arc, and every slug listed resolves to a categories/<slug>.yaml. Note that this file had a schema for a long time before anything applied it; it is a single file rather than a directory, so it fell outside validate's per-directory schema loop and is now checked by a separate call at the end of build/validate.py. The taxonomy descends from the 2024 Columbia Convening on Openness in AI; see docs/methodology.md. docs/reference/openness.md covers how the openness score relates to the same framework.

name.description: The arc's display label — "Model components", "Product / UX", "Infrastructure" — and the human half of the pair `layer` completes. Written by hand here and nowhere else: category files carry no `arc` field, so this string reaches a reader only by way of the arc its category sits in. build/serialize.py copies it onto every category in the arc as `arc`; build/render.py prints it as the small uppercase rule above each notebook section and as the group heading in the at-a-glance roster; the front end (currentai-org/aipotluck.org, web/src/lib/data/loadProducts.ts) uses it as the label on the layer tab, taking it from whichever category in that layer it reaches first. One quirk to know before renaming or splitting an arc: the `{n_layers}` figure in docs/methodology.md is computed in build/render.py from the count of DISTINCT arc names, not from `layer`, so two arcs sharing a layer would render as two sections and be counted as two layers by the prose while `layer_order` deduplicated them to one. Nothing checks that arcs and layers stay one-to-one.

layer.description: Which layer of the Columbia openness ontology (the GPAIS tech stack) this arc IS. The machine half of the arc, where `name` is the label, and the slug every consumer joins on. The three values come from the framework rather than from us, and the map's own prose commits to three ("three layers of the stack" in docs/methodology.md), so adding a fourth is a taxonomy decision rather than a schema edit, and it means editing three places: this enum, the `LAYERS` set hardcoded at build/validate.py:43 that checks the same three a second time so the error can name the offending arc, and the methodology prose. Derived from here and never stored again: build/serialize.py writes it onto each category in the arc and emits the arc sequence as the payload's `layer_order`, which the front end uses to order its layer tabs; build/serialize_registry.py emits it as `categories.layer` for the warehouse. A category file deliberately does not carry its own layer. Stored in two places the two drift, and the arc is the copy that already has to be correct for the display order to work.

categories.description: The category slugs in this arc, in display order. The order is load-bearing: build/serialize.py flattens the arcs in sequence into the payload's `order`, which is the section order in the notebook and the row order in the at-a-glance roster, so moving a slug up here moves that section up. Slugs are underscored (`base_pretrained`) where product and organization slugs are hyphenated, so the two vocabularies cannot be confused at a glance, and each must equal the `name` of a sources/categories/<slug>.yaml — this list carries membership and position only, and everything else about a category lives in that file. Edited by hand alongside creating the category file, and doing only one of the two is the usual mistake, so build/validate.py checks both directions: a slug here with no file, and a category file that appears in zero arcs or in two. Neither check is in the schema, which will accept an empty list or the same slug listed twice.
